blocks.text: What an AI assistant does for an insurance agent

A useful AI assistant for insurance agents does three jobs. It answers questions about the screen in front of you. It drafts text you can review. It handles small everyday tasks, such as calendar entries and reminders. Lazur covers all three on a Mac.

Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask a question. Lazur answers out loud. If you ask where something is, Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. If you ask how to do something, Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click.

It helps to know what it does not do. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or run other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Outlook, Excel or Word. It has no partnership with any app maker. It sits beside your work, not inside it.
Where an insurance agent's day goes

No published study that I could open measures how insurance agents use their computers. The best figures come from all office workers. Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index surveyed 31,000 full-time workers in 31 markets. Those workers spent 57% of their time communicating. Email took 15%, Teams meetings took 23% and Teams chat took 19%.

Email is a large slice, and the heaviest users feel it most. The top 25% of email users spend 8.8 hours a week on email. That number covers all workers. Use it as a warning, not as a benchmark for your agency.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects 572,600 insurance sales agent jobs in 2025. It expects 3% growth from 2025 to 2035, about as fast as the average for all occupations. Median pay in May 2025 was $62,280 a year, or $29.94 an hour.

Every minute spent hunting for a policy number is a minute not spent selling. Track your own week before you decide what to fix. Write down which app is open when each task starts. The pattern shows up fast.
Excel for insurance agents on Mac: renewals and commissions

Renewals are where many agents lose the most time. BLS lists handling policy sales and renewals as a typical duty. A single renewal touches several tools. You check the expiring policy, compare the new quote, email the client and log the result. Each step is small. Together they fill an afternoon.

Excel usually holds the renewal and commission figures. Keep one sheet as the source, and ask Lazur about it instead of hunting through columns. Hold ⌥ ⌘ over the sheet and ask which column holds the commission rate. Lazur circles the header and labels it.

Lazur also explains formulas. Ask what a lookup does in your sheet, and Lazur explains it in plain words. If you want a new formula, ask for one in text. Paste it yourself, then check one row by hand before you trust the rest of the column.
Mistakes happen when a formula copies down into rows with different data. Check the first row, a middle row and the last row. Compare the totals with the carrier statement. The final check is yours.
For a full walk through Excel on a Mac, read [Excel for insurance agents on Mac](/for/insurance-agents/excel).
Outlook for insurance agents on Mac: drafting client emails

Outlook is probably the first app you open each morning. Microsoft's release notes show frequent changes to Outlook for Mac in 2026. Version 16.110 added Import PST on June 16, 2026. Version 16.111 on July 14, 2026 let you pin and reorder left rail modules.

Later releases changed the window layout. Version 16.113 on September 16, 2026 let you right-click Mail, Calendar and People to open each in a separate window. Version 16.114 on October 14, 2026 let supported Office apps appear dynamically in the left rail.

Lazur helps with the drafting, not the sending. Say what the client needs, and Lazur writes a reply in text. You check the names, dates and figures, then send it from Outlook. Never send a draft you have not read.
Lazur works from what is on your screen and what you say. If the client's earlier emails are open, it can use them. If they are not, tell it the facts that matter in one sentence.

For the setup of Outlook, see [Outlook for insurance agents on Mac](/for/insurance-agents/outlook). For a calendar entry, [create a calendar event in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/create-a-calendar-event-in-outlook) walks you through the steps.
Legacy Outlook for Mac and Exchange Online: check your version
Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. The reason is that the EWS service it uses retires on October 1, 2026.

That October date has now passed. Open Outlook and confirm which version you run. Legacy Outlook for Mac keeps working with Exchange On-Premises mailboxes until October 9, 2029, but it gets only security updates in that time. Standalone or App Store versions are not supported for legacy Outlook.
If the old client still opens your Exchange Online mail, ask your IT contact or agency tech lead for the plan. Do not wait for an error to tell you. Ask now, while you can still plan the switch.
Dictation and file notes for insurance agents

Hold fn to dictate. Lazur types clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Save names and carrier terms in your personal dictionary, so the spelling comes out right. Snippets and clipboard slots handle the lines you repeat, such as your standard disclosure paragraph.
Dictate the summary of a call, then type the policy number yourself. Speech tools miss numbers and unusual names. Read the note back before you save it to the client file.

To test how well your voice comes through, try the [dictation accuracy checker](/tools/dictation-accuracy-checker). Then compare your speaking and typing speed with the [speaking versus typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test).
Agency management systems on a Mac: what to confirm first

Your agency system matters more than your email app. HawkSoft's requirements list Windows 11 and Windows Server 2016 or newer. They also list 8 GB of memory as the minimum. HawkSoft lists 'Limited support for macOS' and says HawkSoft on macOS 'will require third-party services'.

Applied Systems' Epic Browser hub says the product works with Windows and Mac workstations. For the browser on a Mac, it says you 'must have a program such as Parallels installed.' Its page lists Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox and Microsoft Edge as supported browsers. An older Applied FAQ reportedly says Apple products are not supported. I could not open it, so confirm with Applied.

Ask your vendor three things. Does the system run on a Mac natively or through Parallels? Which browser does it need? Does it depend on a third-party service you must pay for? Write the answers down before you rely on any tool.

Lazur sees whatever your Mac displays, including a window from Parallels. Test it once with a harmless screen before a client file is open. A virtual machine adds a layer, so check that both your question and the answer work.
Client data and your agency's rules

Client files hold personal and financial details. Your duties come from your agency, your carriers and your state's licensing rules. This page cannot say which rules bind you. Ask your manager or compliance lead before you put client data into any AI tool.

Here is how Lazur handles data, as Lazur describes it. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
That description does not decide what your agency allows. A rule from your agency always wins. If the agency bans AI tools near client files, do not hold the shortcut while a client file is open.

A simple habit helps. Ask for the menu, the button or the wording, and leave identifying details out of the question. For example, ask 'How do I attach a file in Outlook?' instead of reading out a client's full file.
A worked example: one renewal from start to finish
Here is a homeowners renewal with a small coverage change. Your agency's process may differ, so use this as a pattern, not a rule.

blocks.text: Notice the split. You make the decisions on coverage, price and whether the change fits the client. Lazur handles lookups, wording and reminders. The judgment stays with you, and that is the point.
Mistakes agents make with an AI assistant

items: Expecting Lazur to click. It points, explains and guides. You click.
Sending a draft without reading it. Names, dates and figures are where errors hide.
Trusting a dictated policy number. Read it back against the source document.
Skipping the agency rule because the tool is fast.
Asking one big question for a whole workflow. Ask about one step at a time.
Assuming the tool knows the client. It only knows what is on screen and what you say.

blocks.text: When an AI assistant is the wrong tool

Lazur is the wrong tool for a decision that needs your license, your judgment or the carrier's rules. Use the policy form for coverage questions. Use your underwriter or manager when a risk falls outside your guidelines.

Research is different. Lazur runs research in its own Chrome tabs and returns a summary and a report. Check each claim against the carrier's own page before a client sees it. Do not treat a summary as the source.
Also check the screen. If the window is hidden, minimized or inside a remote session that does not show on your Mac, Lazur cannot read it. Bring the window forward, then hold the shortcut.
How to start this week
Pick one task you repeat. Renewal emails and Excel lookups are good first choices. Time how long it takes for a few days. Then decide whether Lazur saves real time.

Download Lazur from the [download page](/download). The trial starts when you first open the app, and it needs no credit card. Compare the Pro and Power plans on [pricing](/pricing) before you pay for anything.

Then read the agent guides for [Outlook](/for/insurance-agents/outlook) and [Excel](/for/insurance-agents/excel). For mail basics, see [how to create a folder in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/create-a-folder-in-outlook).
Where these numbers come from
I did not find a study that measures insurance agents' computer time directly. The time figures here come from all office workers. The job figures come from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

BLS lists 'Maintain client records' as a duty. Its page does not mention paperwork or computers. The admin load on agents is therefore inferred, not measured. Treat the numbers as context for your own week, not as proof of it.
Outlook dates and version numbers come from Microsoft's release notes and support pages. Check them again before you plan a switch, because Microsoft updates these pages often.

faq.question: What is an AI assistant for insurance agents on a Mac?
faq.answer: It is a voice assistant that answers questions about what is on your screen and drafts text for you to review. Lazur is one example. It does not click buttons, edit files or run other apps for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Outlook, Excel and Word?
faq.answer: It works with anything that shows on your screen, including Outlook, Excel and Word. It is not a plugin or add-in for those apps, and it has no partnership with their makers.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Applied Epic or HawkSoft?
faq.answer: Lazur reads what your Mac displays. Whether the agency system runs on your Mac is up to the vendor. Applied says a Mac needs Parallels or a similar program for its browser. HawkSoft lists limited macOS support. Confirm with each vendor first.

faq.question: Can I use an AI assistant with client data?
faq.answer: Only if your agency allows it. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer and are not stored. Your agency's rules still decide what is allowed.

faq.question: Will an AI assistant replace the admin work?
faq.answer: It cuts lookup and wording time. It does not replace your judgment on coverage or price. BLS says agents 'will still be needed to help clients understand their options.'

faq.question: Which Macs does Lazur run on?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available yet.

faq.question: How much does Lazur cost?
faq.answer: There is a free trial that starts when you first open the app, with no credit card. Pro and Power plans are listed on the pricing page. Check the current prices there before you buy.

faq.question: How do I tell which Outlook I am running?
faq.answer: Open Outlook and check the version under Outlook > About Outlook. If you still run legacy Outlook against Exchange Online, ask IT for the plan. Microsoft set October 2026 for that change, and that month has now passed.
